# Game compatibility

<!-- Generated from patches/<Game>/game.ini by tools/dev/gen-compatibility.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

This list shows what has been tried so far, on one setup (a Steam Deck with a PS Move ZCM1 and a PS3 Eye). It is a snapshot, not a promise: arcade games differ a lot, and some depend on the TeknoParrot runtime or on your own dump.
RavenGun ships no games. You need your own legally obtained copies.

## Working (47)

These games run on RavenGun's own loader and start straight from RavenGun (double-click), without TeknoParrot; they were played with the lightgun (PS Move or mouse) and checked on the TV. The note says what was tested.

- **Aliens Extermination**: WORKING (2026-10-17, played in mouse mode for 5.5 min: high scores, press start, mission select by shooting, aiming and shooting in the game). Starts by double-click (2026-10-17): PeFillPages (the HASP emulation behind .text that Wine cleared), gamescope with Windowed = 1 at 1920x1080: boot screen, Global VR and PlayMechanix logos, attract with free play / press start. Open: the boot screen reports no GVRIO card and no Aliens guns; input not measured yet.

## Playable (4)

These games start from RavenGun and can be played with the lightgun. Some are not yet confirmed with a real PS Move in every detail; the note says what was tested.

- **Gashaaaan Refill!!!!**: Playable after a one-time setup in the test menu (clock, screen, free play; now stored in the game's save data). Then start, aiming and trigger (the ball) work. Test menu: key 0, select with start, execute with P1 aux1.
- **Go Go Strike**: Works: bowling with the Move as trackball (direction and swing set the throw), start (key 1) and trigger (click). 4:3 picture with black bars (gamescope).
- **Luigi's Mansion Arcade**: Starts by double-click in RavenGun (2026-10-14): on our own OpenParrot core and through gamescope the game runs full screen in attract (with the closed core it stopped after ~13 s). Measured earlier: ~6 min of continuous attract/demo on our core (BEWIJS-5MIN.md), with the drop-in rg-pe-hook.dll (see MECHANISME-PE-HOOK.md). NOT playable yet: coin and TEST do not reach the game (DIRECT-ROUTE-INVOER.md).
- **Target Bravo: Operation G.H.O.S.T.**: MEASURED 2026-10-21 14:20-14:35 (headless, claude-tnx). CALIBRATION: the factory values in CONTROLLER ADJUSTMENT (gs2.exe -testmode, service = F3, test = 0) are for the cabinet's 1024x600 gun: aiming at the picture centre gave ADJUSTED 523,213 in the game's 1024x768 space, i.e. about 15 px right and 240 px high on a 1080p screen. After the game's own procedure (aim at each green cross with ravengunctl test-pattern point and pull the trigger: TOP 38, LEFT 49, RIGHT 973, BOTTOM 429, CENTER 511,234, EXIT (WITH SAVE)) the CHECK marker lands within 1 px of the aim at the centre, (0.2,0.5), (0.8,0.5) and the four points (0.25/0.75, 0.15/0.85) (shots-tnx/k*.png); in a later normal run the mode select followed the aim (WAVE picked at 0.73,0.5). Seeded as seed/mxeeprom.bin. INPUT TEST: our reload bit is the board's SCREEN OUT (reload -> SCREEN OUT), grenade -> ACTION; CHANGE has no mapping. RELOAD in a mission: reload held + trigger refilled 06 -> 24; aiming at the screen edge (0.0) + trigger just fired (09 -> 06), because board SegaGun2P fed the SCREEN OUT bit from the reload button only. - **Coopers's 9**: 2026-10-21: the 2026-10-17 "PLEASE CALIBRATE THE GUN" start was on the closed TeknoParrot core (the profile had no [Loader] section then). With our own path the exe looked unstartable because game.exe is a flat memory image whose section table still points at the packed original: the import directory (RVA 0x27297c0, inside .protect) was read 0x10a000 bytes early and looked empty. After tools/dev/pe-flat-fix.py the import table parses (15 descriptors: KERNEL32, SETUPAPI, USER32, d3d9, DINPUT8, DSOUND, WINMM, GDI32, ADVAPI32, ole32, OLEAUT32, MSVCR71; names read from the dump itself), Wine loads all of them plus our d3d9 (DXVK) and DINPUT8, and the process runs ~40 s with no exception (the old 0x4fd8aed0 crash is gone), then exits with code 0. No picture yet. Reference run on the closed core (2026-10-21 07:26, installed profile with the [Loader] section removed, gamescope headless): the unchanged NAS exe does show its own "PLEASE CALIBRATE THE GUN" screen, so the closed core is what makes this dump run. What our own path lacks: the game does not call the descriptor imports directly, it jumps through a second table at 0x512000 in .rdata (49 thunks over 47 slots; no descriptor FirstThunk; slots hold XP addresses and 0x0313xxxx stubs of protection memory the dump does not contain). Slot 0x5123a0 holds 0x4FD8AED0 - the exact address of every crash measured - and it is the first call after static init (entry 0x402480 -> 0x4010d0 -> jmp [0x5123a0]). That table has to be rebuilt slot by slot from the game own code; reading it from a reference run is blocked by kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1.

- **After Dark**: READ 2026-10-21 (static, on our own view copy): the gate is one branch. Window procedure path of GameLaunch: 0x406474 call 0x415ca0 -> 0x406479 test al,al -> 0x40647b jne 0x4064a2 (continue); the fall-through at 0x40647d pushes MB_ICONHAND with caption "GameLaunch" (0x7d12b4) and text "Init Dongle Failed !" (0x7d1a78) and returns false. 0x415ca0 itself: it creates the ATL object (0x415b30, stored at 0x8987b0), then walks a fixed array of object slots at 0x8983b0 (0x400 bytes = up to 0x100 dwords, slots released and cleared on failure) and for each slot calls vtable [0x1c], then a pair with [0x14](obj, out, "InsGame", 0) and [0x10](obj, &slot, out), then [0x58](obj, "3DGame", 6) and [0x10](obj, &slot, out); ebx counts the slots that passed and AL is what the caller tests. "InsGame" and "3DGame" are ATL property names, so the dongle is read as a property bag by name, not as a serial number we could guess. Measured under plain Wine (+file, no board): hid.dll is loaded from system32 and the trace has no access to \\.\ITOKEN2 at all in that early run, so the first failure is a property read, before any device I/O. MEASURED 2026-10-21 08:26 (full recipe: rg-direct --run of the plan, gamescope headless, rg-compat loaded, "Have fun :)"): with the unpatched exe the game sits idle at the dongle gate (0.6 % CPU after a minute) -- that is the "Init Dongle Failed !" box. Then one byte at 0x40647b was changed in a local copy of the exe (75 -> EB, "jne success" becomes "jmp success"; the old bytes were checked first) and that copy was put in the view in place of the symlink for one run (symlink restored afterwards): the game does NOT crash and does NOT show the box, it exits with code 0 within seconds. So skipping that single gate is not enough -- the dongle object has to answer its properties, otherwise the game shuts itself down. NEXT: read the ATL property map of the class behind 0x415b30 to get every property name with its type and the value each slot is asked for, then answer them (device/ATL stub) or patch this one gate -- one byte at 0x40647b (75 25 -> eb 25) forces the success branch, but the success path dereferences 0x8983b0, so it is only safe once the object exists. READ FURTHER 2026-10-21 09:15 (static, own view copy): the dongle object is ATL CComObject<CCoDongle2> with interface ICoDongle2; its constructor is 0x415930 (allocates 0x30 bytes from 0x415b30) and it stores the vtable 0x7d3ca4, which holds 17 entries (QueryInterface 0x4159c0, AddRef, Release 0x415990, then 0x492e20, 0x40af60, 0x40a7b0, 0x40a890, 0x40a5f0, 0x40ab90, 0x415ad0, 0x84402c, 0x415c80, 0x415bf0, 0x415c00, 0x7027d0, 0x415c10, 0x415c60). What 0x415ca0 and the success path ask of it: [vt+0x1c](this), then per slot of up to 0x100 at 0x8983b0 "[vt+0x14](this,&out,\"InsGame\",0) then [vt+0x10](this,&slot,&out)" and "[vt+0x58](this,\"3DGame\",6) then [vt+0x10](this,&slot,&out)"; after the gate, 0x4064a2 does [vt+0x10], [vt+0x30](this,&local), [vt+0x50](this,0,&buf,8,0x42) -- an 8-byte dongle read with mode 0x42 -- and then starts a thread (0x415850 with proc 0x415560) and sets 0x439168(this,\"InsGame\",1). NOTE: +0x50 and +0x58 lie outside the 17-entry vtable of CComObject<CCoDongle2>, so the object the game holds is the ATL aggregate/contained wrapper; that wrapper (and therefore the real member functions the names go to) is the next thing to pin down. The device is addressed by a 16-byte id: 0x436260 compares four dwords against a table at 0x874e00 and returns the name "ITOKEN2" (0x7d4bfc); the strings "UserBB Dongle" (0x7d2790, used at 0x40c4d2 and 0x40c702) and "Dongle Auth" (0x7d27b8, used at 0x40c72f) belong to a dongle status dialog worth reading for the values it expects. PLAN: log the real call sequence with a small 32-bit drop-in that hooks CreateFileA/DeviceIoControl/ReadFile for the ITOKEN2 name (the rg-rhio pattern) and answer it from what the code above checks, then patch the getter by patchmem only for values that cannot be produced. READ 2026-10-21 09:20: the object the game really calls has a 28-entry vtable at 0x7d2564 (methods in the 0x40b-0x40c range, next to the "UserBB Dongle"/"Dongle Auth" strings), not the 17-entry 0x7d3ca4 of CComObject<CCoDongle2> -- so the game holds an ATL wrapper whose interface adds the methods 0x415ca0 uses. The two named calls are RECORD READS, not flags: [vt+0x14] is 0x40b860, which rejects a size above 0x18 (E_INVALIDARG 0x80070057) and copies up to 24 bytes into the caller buffer, and [vt+0x58] is 0x40bab0, which rejects a size above 8 and copies up to 8 bytes. - **Sega Game Shell**: MEASURED 2026-10-19 13:55 (item G): the shell STARTS and DRAWS on RavenGun's own loader and core. Shell.exe is a 32-bit Windows app; it runs through RavenGun's OpenParrot loader with Core = ravengun, without DXVK (it draws its own screen), in the view that belongs to it. The screenshot (docs/screenshots/segamegameshell-game-error-2026-10-19.png) shows the shell's own screen: "Game Shell / Version 180605 / GAME ERROR". So the start, loading the exe and drawing are fine, but the shell reports an error itself because this folder holds no game for it -- GameData only has "compiled" and the folder otherwise holds the shell and Transformers2 (which has its own profile). Needed in this round: an own profile (there was only an empty template), a view with the exe's directory as a REAL directory (otherwise the engine does not find the game in the view), writable directories (ViewWritable) for ShellData, temp and shell/variables, and an Input route (tp-shm with WartranTroopers) because the engine otherwise picks the evdev route. Correction 2026-10-19 (review 16): "find" does not see DELETIONS and the bwrap writelayer hides the writes, so "0 new files" proved nothing. The 13:45 start deleted 157 old "Attract - 2610xx.log" files in shell/ and wrote shell/variables/erlg(.bak); the writelayer holds 157 whiteouts and 2 files for that. Correction 2026-10-19 (pass 2): Wine deletes and renames THROUGH a file link (wineserver works with the real path), so those deletes hit the files on the NAS, not the links in the view. Only the bwrap writelayer kept the NAS intact (209 log files are still there); a bare rg-direct --run without that layer would have deleted them. That is why shell/ is now in ViewLocalFiles: at start every file link in shell/ becomes a local copy, Graphics and Sounds stay links, and a bare rg-direct --run refuses while a file link to the NAS remains in shell/. Next step: find out what the shell needs to find a game (GameData/compiled or a licence file) and whether the Transformers2 folder is one it should start.
